Chapter 213: 0210 A Certain Mr. Feng Comes to Game Science?

Like the major blog sites, Kaixin Net had many reporters staked out on it.

These reporters didn't do much else all day. They just squatted on various websites, browsing all kinds of online articles. Then they'd summarize the key points and write them up as news, or simply reprint the original text in newspapers and magazines.

When the microblog post with the photo of Chen Guiliang and Chen Xiaoxu was published, many reporters received text message alerts and immediately flooded Chen Xiaoxu's personal homepage.

Chen Xiaoxu hadn't written a single word or posted a single picture, yet she was about to be reported on by numerous gossip magazines.

Her whole family was living in the capital at this time. She lived with her husband, while her parents lived in another apartment. When she got home in the afternoon and turned on her computer, she found that many netizens had come to leave messages on her message board.

So, Chen Xiaoxu wrote a journal entry. The gist of it was that she was doing very well and thanked the vast number of netizens for their concern and support.

When she refreshed a few minutes later, there was a huge pile of comments.

She found it quite interesting and replied to everyone earnestly.

But the comments just kept coming, and it was impossible to reply to them all. In the end, she had no choice but to give up and leave it be.

She stopped paying attention to the comments and instead sent a text message to top up her account, buying some items to decorate her little online den. First, she painted the house, then she had to put up wallpaper, followed by all sorts of furniture and appliances.

She even bought an electronic cat and an electronic dog as pets.

Chen Xiaoxu didn't tell any of her real-life friends, just playing on Kaixin Net by herself. But she didn't get the hang of the mini-games because she had no friends to interact with. She was just foolishly planting vegetables on her own.

In a few more days, after the print media reported on it, some of her real-life friends would probably show up.

The moment Chen Xiaoxu left ByteDance, Xie Yang came over, filled with regret, "I was too embarrassed to ask for an autograph just now."

"You don't seem to watch *Dream of the Red Chamber*, do you?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Xie Yang said, "I've just never watched a full episode, but I often saw clips during the summer vacation."

"And you call yourself a fan?" Chen Guiliang was speechless.

Xie Yang chuckled and changed the subject, "Teacher Zheng Yuanjie has joined Kaixin Net. Just an hour ago, our promotion staff cornered him at the entrance to his residential complex."

Chen Guiliang couldn't help but laugh. "Are you guys stalking people now?"

Xie Yang said, "You have no idea. Zheng Yuanjie is a perfect fit for Kaixin Net! He recently joined Sina Blog, but he doesn't write a single proper article. He just talks about what he did all day. He even brings up trivial matters. This morning, he posted on his blog bright and early, saying he was planning to go out and buy groceries."

"If that's really the case, he is indeed more suited for Kaixin Net," Chen Guiliang said with a smile.

What Zheng Yuanjie was playing at was online interaction, not the one-way output of a blog.

Staying on Sina Blog was a complete waste of his talent.

Xie Yang said, "He's posted photos on his blog before, so we had long since figured out which residential complex he lives in. This morning when he said he was going to buy groceries, I immediately sent people over, and they caught him right on his way back. Our people carefully explained Kaixin Net's model, and as expected, he was willing to come over after hearing about it."

After a bit more conversation, Chen Guiliang returned to his office.

He called Game Science downstairs. "How are the talks with JJ Lin going?"

Qu Guohao said, "His agent is asking for an 8 million yuan endorsement fee."

"For 8 million, I could sign a non-exclusive deal with Jay Chou!" Chen Guiliang was a little ticked off, because the asking price was just too ridiculous.

Qu Guohao said, "I plan to let it cool off for a bit. We can't be hasty at a time like this. The more anxious we are, the less they'll budge."

Chen Guiliang instructed, "If it really doesn't work out, just buy the in-game broadcasting rights for *Cao Cao* and *Tale of the Three Kingdoms*."

"Okay," Qu Guohao said.

During this period, Game Science was very busy.

On one hand, they were busy with the qualifying rounds for the second National Collegiate League for *Legends of the Three Kingdoms*; on the other, they were busy organizing exclusive *Legends of the Three Kingdoms* activities for "World Online Game Day."

March 21st this year was the first World Online Game Day.

All game companies in mainland China were to hold various activities for this day.

The sponsors of this festival, aside from 17173, included the GAPP, the Game Working Committee, and the Working Committee for the Care of the Next Generation.

Creating a festival specifically for online games was also considered caring for the next generation.

To cater to this festival, new games were rushing to launch, namely *Eudemons Online* and *Crazyracing Kartrider*.

The competition in the online game market was getting more and more intense!

Chen Guiliang turned on his computer, clicked on a web portal, and carefully browsed the latest news from the Two Sessions.

The hot topics at this year's Two Sessions were mainly: the "Three Rural Issues," construction of the rule of law, and narrowing the gap between rich and poor.

Last year, migrant workers demanding back pay had led to two bloody incidents that shocked the nation. Before the Spring Festival, all regions across the country were helping migrant workers collect their wages, afraid that something else might happen.

This year, the central government directly issued a long document demanding the resolution of the problem of unpaid wages for migrant workers.

Additionally, the construction of a new socialist countryside began this year, and the agricultural tax was officially abolished on New Year's Day.

Chen Guiliang carefully read every news article about the Two Sessions, trying to connect the policy spirit with his own memories.

After reading for a while, his head started to ache. Chen Guiliang exited the web portal and went to follow Zheng Yuanjie's Kaixin Net account, only to find that his homepage was quiet and empty.

With nothing better to do, Chen Guiliang left a message, "Uncle Zheng Yuanjie, do you ever procrastinate on your manuscripts? I've been dragging out my publisher for a year now."

Zheng Yuanjie was decorating his online den. He only saw the message a few minutes later and immediately replied, "Writing that comes from procrastination is what you'd call a full-term, natural birth. Let them develop a while longer in the mother's womb."

"If they develop any longer, they'll turn into Nezha," Chen Guiliang replied.

Zheng Yuanjie said, "Then have the publisher raise the price."

"They can't. My royalty is 20%, the highest in all of China."

"Showing off to me, are you? I'm off to cook!"

"Let's follow each other. We can add each other as friends if we're mutuals."

Zheng Yuanjie didn't go to cook. Instead, he Googled "Chen Guiliang" and was overwhelmed by the sheer number of web pages that popped up.

Too lazy to continue browsing, he casually followed Chen Guiliang and they added each other as friends.

Then he picked up his phone, went to the kitchen to take a picture of the vegetables he had just bought, and posted a microblog about what delicious meal he was going to make.

This "King of Fairy Tales" was truly a perfect fit for Kaixin Net and microblogging!

Ao Yanchen was getting more and more skilled at managing the company. Chen Guiliang, sitting in his office, actually felt a bit idle.

He simply got up from his computer and strolled downstairs to Game Science.

Time to check on the game's development progress!

The name for the side-scrolling game had been decided. It was called *Next Age*, with the English abbreviation *NA*.

The development team was named "Next Studio."

Including Shuxia Yehu, who was in charge of story planning, the studio now had 16 members.

"Boss Chen!"

"Boss."

As Chen Guiliang walked into the studio, several members stood up one after another.

The lead planner was named Meng Zicong. He was recommended by an employee from Pixel Software, and Chen Guiliang had poached him from Object Software. This person had participated in the engine development for *Prince of Qin II*.

Well, *Prince of Qin II* ended up in development hell.

It caused a bunch of developers to leave, including the person who would later become the development lead for *Tian Long Ba Bu*.

"Boss Chen!" Bao Junzhe greeted him excitedly.

"You've already started?" Chen Guiliang nodded with a smile.

This Bao Junzhe was the Zhejiang University student who had shown up at the *Legends of the Three Kingdoms* competition before the Spring Festival. He had zero game development experience but had a solid technical foundation.

Chen Guiliang asked, "How's the progress?"

Meng Zicong explained, "We've already created the core engine and a playable prototype. We're currently verifying the fundamental feasibility of its combat feel. We're about to enter the next phase."

Chen Guiliang leaned over to the computer and saw only two crude, humanoid blobs.

Meng Zicong sat down and operated it for a bit. The two humanoid blobs started fighting, and you could faintly get a sense of the combat feel.

Chen Guiliang then asked Hu Geng, Shuxia Yehu, "How's the story design coming along?"

Hu Geng said, "The framework was completed long ago, and the plot and scenes for each level are almost designed. I'm planning to start writing the novel and serializing it online next month."

"Very fast," Chen Guiliang nodded in approval.

After a tour of the studio, Chen Guiliang couldn't be of much help and could only ask about the employees' well-being. Finally, he said, "Once you guys have a semi-finished product, I'll invite that kid who's amazing at King of Fighters to come test your combat system."

"That would be great," Meng Zicong said with a smile.

Chen Guiliang strolled out of the studio, and an employee followed him out.

He caught up to him in the hallway and said hesitantly, "Boss..."

"Go ahead, what is it," Chen Guiliang said.

The employee was still stammering, "I have a classmate who's looking for a job... he..."

Chen Guiliang said, "Tell me about his resume."

The employee found it hard to say. "He's like me, a graduate from Huazhong University of Science and Technology. But... he studied biomedical engineering, and after graduating with his bachelor's, he worked at the Institute of Biophysics, Chinese Academy of Sciences, for a while..."

"Someone who studied biomedical engineering wants to join Game Science to make games?" Chen Guiliang felt that something wasn't quite right.

The employee quickly explained, "He has a great passion for the gaming industry. He even gave up on grad school for games."

It was true passion. He gave up grad school, gave up his job at the Chinese Academy of Sciences, and then spent all day in internet cafes playing *World of Warcraft*. He played until he ran out of living expenses and had to borrow money from all his classmates. Now he was forced to leave the internet cafe to find a job.

He was working odd jobs while still hanging out at internet cafes.

Chen Guiliang asked, "What's his name?"

The employee said, "Feng Ji."

Chen Guiliang took a few seconds to process it before making a very pertinent assessment, "That name is a perfect fit for our Game Science. Let him join Next Studio as a general helper. We'll see what kind of work he can adapt to."

"Huh?" The employee thought he had misheard.

He was only asking on behalf of Feng Ji because they were classmates, and he never expected Chen Guiliang to agree directly.

Chen Guiliang explained, "He didn't go to grad school, didn't stay at the Chinese Academy of Sciences, just to go play games. A person like that has a real passion for gaming. I can give him a chance."

The employee said happily, "Thank you, Boss."

After Chen Guiliang left, the employee took out his phone and called Feng Ji. "Damn it, are you still playing Warcraft? Stop fucking playing and hurry up and come to Game Science for work... I'm not kidding, Boss Chen agreed... Hurry, right now! Remember to change into some clean clothes. Damn, you smelled rancid the last time I saw you."

Standing in the elevator, Chen Guiliang thought to himself: Could it be that because I named the company Game Science, I ended up attracting the man himself?

It was just so damn metaphysical.

(End of this chapter)
